caveats.message: Factor 'position': assignment.method is 'inherent' in the declaration (Position is a property of the measurement location.). The tests and intervals are computed the same way for every assignment method; the caveat concerns attributing a difference to the factor (D-039).

explanation.text: The declaration says this factor's levels were not assigned at random: they were assigned systematically, the method was not stated, or the factor is an inherent property such as a position on the wafer. The test and intervals are computed the same way regardless. What changes is the interpretation: without randomization, a difference may partly reflect something else that varied along with the factor, so it should not automatically be read as caused by it.

fit.method: closed-form order-restricted (pool-adjacent-violators) REML for balanced designs; no optimizer, so no convergence failure (D-064)
fit.fixed_parameterization: cell means: one indicator per whole-plot x subplot cell
fit.convention: -2 log L_R = (N - p) log(2 pi) + sum_k [ df_k log lambda_k + SS_k / lambda_k ] + log det(X'X), the standard restricted log-likelihood (Harville 1977). The last term is an additive constant that depends on how the fixed effects are parameterised, so a REML log-likelihood is comparable only between fits that share one. X here is the full-rank indicator parameterisation named in `fixed_parameterization`. The form without that term is also reported, and any offset against a package's printed value is reported rather than absorbed (D-064).

fits.note: Every step is closed form (exact rational ANOVA, closed-form REML, deterministic quantile functions), so no fit can fail to converge. An empty `failed` list means none occurred, not that none were looked for (D-066). A design the evidence checks refuse is not a failed fit: refusal is a successful outcome.

notes: etch_setting is applied to whole wafers, so the only replication it has is the 3 wafers per level: it is tested on (3, 8) df against whole-plot error, and the denominator df count a(r - 1) = 4 x (3 - 1) = 8.

position and etch_setting x position vary inside a whole plot, so every whole plot contributes its own comparison: they are tested against subplot error on a(r - 1)(b - 1) = 4 x (3 - 1) x (4 - 1) = 24 df.
That is why the two factors have different denominator degrees of freedom even though they come from the same 48 readings: they are replicated at different levels of the design.
The naive single-error analysis is reported beside the correct one and is labelled wrong for this design (brief Section 5.3).
